extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies' regulatory/publication officers; Office of the Federal Register staff; agency liaison/certifying/authorizing officers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for federal agencies to prepare, submit, publish, and distribute documents in the Federal Register, the Code of Federal Regulations, and related special editions (e.g., Government Manual, Public Papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Index to daily issues (§6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each daily issue of the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be appropriately indexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily issues must include appropriate indexing to assist users in locating content published in that issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical subject indexes (§6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analytical subject indexes covering the contents of the FEDERAL REGISTER shall be published as currently as practicable and shall be cumulated and separately published at least once each calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexes should be kept as current as practicable and produced in cumulative form at least annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily numerical list of parts affected (§6.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each daily issue of the FEDERAL REGISTER shall carry a numerical list of the parts of the Code of Federal Regulations specifically affected by documents published in that issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every daily issue must include a numerical list identifying CFR parts affected by that issue's documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly cumulated list of parts affected (§6.3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with the second issue of each month, each daily issue shall also carry a cumulated list of the parts affected by documents published during that month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the second issue onward each month, daily issues must include a cumulative monthly list of affected CFR parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly list of sections affected (§6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A monthly list of sections of the Code of Federal Regulations affected shall be separately published on a cumulative basis during each calendar year. The list shall identify the sections of the Code specifically affected by documents published in the FEDERAL REGISTER during the period it covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a separate cumulative monthly list identifying CFR sections affected by FR publications for the covered period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexes, digests, and guides (§6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may order the preparation and publication of indexes, digests, and similar guides ... which will serve users of the FEDERAL REGISTER. Indexes, digests, and similar guides will be published yearly or at other intervals as necessary to keep them current and useful. Each index, digest, and guide is considered to be a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER whenever the public need requires special printing or special binding in substantial numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may issue subject guides as needed; they should be maintained current (yearly or as necessary) and may be designated special editions when special printing/binding in substantial numbers is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for the Code of Federal Regulations (§8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to chapter 15 of title 44, United States Code, the Director of the Federal Register shall publish periodically a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER to present a compact and practical code called the 'Code of Federal Regulations', to contain each Federal regulation of general applicability and legal effect. The Administrative Committee intends that every practical means be used to keep the Code as current and readily usable as possible, within limitations imposed by dependability and reasonable costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFR must be a compact, practical code of all general-effect regulations and kept as current/readily usable as practicable while balancing dependability and reasonable cost constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderly development of CFR (§8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: To assure orderly development of the Code of Federal Regulations along practical lines, the Director of the Federal Register may establish new titles in the Code and rearrange existing titles and subordinate assignments. However, before taking an action under this section, the Director shall consult with each agency directly affected by the proposed change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may reorganize CFR titles but must consult each directly affected agency before doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic updating of CFR (§8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria. Each book of the Code shall be updated at least once each calendar year. If no change in its contents has occurred during the year, a simple notation to that effect may serve as the supplement for that year. More frequent updating of any unit of the Code may be made whenever the Director of the Federal Register determines that the content of the unit has been substantially superseded or otherwise determines that such action would be consistent with the intent and purpose ... Staggered publication: The Code will be produced over a 12-month period under a staggered publication system ... Cutoff dates: Each updated title of the Code will reflect each amendment to that title published as a codified regulation in the FEDERAL REGISTER on or before the 'As of' date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update each CFR book at least annually (notation allowed if no changes). Use staggered 12-month publication. Each updated title reflects amendments published on or before its 'As of' cutoff date; Director may update more frequently when content is substantially superseded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject index to the Code (§8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject index to the entire Code shall be annually revised and separately published. An agency-prepared index for any individual book may be published with the approval of the Director of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce and publish an annually revised subject index to the entire CFR; agency-prepared individual-book indexes require Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillaries: parallel tables of statutory authorities and rules (§8.5(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parallel tables of statutory authorities and rules. Numerical lists of all sections of the current edition of the United States Code ... which are cited by issuing agencies as rulemaking authority for currently effective regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations. The lists shall be arranged in the order of the titles and sections of the United States Code ... with parallel citations to the pertinent titles and parts of the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide parallel statutory-authority tables linking U.S. Code sections (orderly by title/section) to CFR titles/parts where cited as rulemaking authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillaries: parallel tables of Presidential documents and agency rules (§8.5(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Code of Federal Regulations Index ... tables of proclamations, Executive orders, and similar Presidential documents which are cited as rulemaking authority in currently effective regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include parallel tables connecting Presidential documents (proclamations, Executive orders, etc.) to CFR regulations that cite them as authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillaries: list of CFR sections affected (§8.5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the text of each Code of Federal Regulations volume, a numerical list of sections which are affected by documents published in the FEDERAL REGISTER. Listings shall refer to FEDERAL REGISTER pages and shall be designed to enable the user of the Code to find the precise text that was in effect on a given date in the period covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each CFR volume must include a numerical list of sections affected by FR documents, with FR page citations to allow users to locate the exact text effective on a given date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of publication (§8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee authorizes publication of the Code of Federal Regulations in the following formats: (1) Paper; (2) Microfiche; and (3) Online on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101). The Director of the Federal Register is authorized to regulate the format of the Code ... may provide for the Code ... to be printed in as many separately bound books as necessary, set requirements for microfiche images, and oversee the organization and means of access to material in the online edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFR may be published in paper, microfiche, and online; Director may regulate formats, binding, microfiche requirements, and online organization to meet user needs and GPO compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency cooperation in keeping CFR current (§8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall cooperate in keeping publication of the Code current by complying promptly with deadlines set by the Director of the Federal Register and the Public Printer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must promptly meet Director/Public Printer deadlines to assist in maintaining current CFR publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of citation (§8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code of Federal Regulations may be cited by title and section, and the short form 'CFR' may be used for 'Code of Federal Regulations.' For example, '1 CFR 10.2' refers to title 1, Code of Federal Regulations, part 10, section 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use title and section citation format; 'CFR' is acceptable as short form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of the United States Government Manual (§9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director publishes a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER called 'The United States Government Manual' as authorized by the Administrative Committee. The Director may update the Manual when such supplementation is considered to be in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce the Manual as a special edition and update as public interest warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Government Manual (§9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Manual will contain appropriate information about the Executive, Legislative, and Judicial branches of the Federal Government, which for the major Executive agencies will include descriptions of the agency's legal authorities, public purposes, programs, and functions; established places and methods whereby the public may obtain information and make submittals or requests; lists of officials heading major operating units. The Manual will also contain brief information about quasi-official agencies and supplemental information that ... is of enough public interest to warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual content must include agency descriptions, public access methods, lists of officials, and brief info on quasi-official agencies and other supplemental materials deemed of public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents publication (§10.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director publishes a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER compiling recent presidential documents, called 'The Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a daily compilation of presidential documents as a special edition of the FR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and sources for Daily Compilation (§10.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the publication consists of oral statements by the President or of writing subscribed by the President, and selected from transcripts or text issued by the Office of the White House Press Secretary, including communications to Congress; public addresses and remarks; news conferences and interviews; public messages and letters; statements released on miscellaneous subjects; and formal executive documents promulgated in accordance with law. In addition, each publication includes selections ... when issued by the Press Office (appointments and nominations; White House statements and announcements; statements by the Press Secretary or Deputy Press Secretary; statements and news conferences by senior administration officials; and fact sheets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include primary presidential statements and selected related White House Press Office material as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for Daily Compilation (§10.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents is published online on the Government Printing Office access system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily Compilation is published online via GPO Access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Papers of the Presidents: annual publication (§10.10–10.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall publish annually a special edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER called the 'Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States.' The basic text consists of the documents compiled under subpart A (Daily Compilation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish an annual compilation (Public Papers) that collects the daily-compiled presidential documents for the year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, indexes, and ancillaries for Public Papers (§10.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication covers one calendar year, unless procedures require otherwise, and is divided into books according to the amount of material to be included. The publication is published in the binding and style that the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register considers suitable to the dignity of the Office of the President of the United States. Each publication is appropriately indexed and contains additional ancillary information and illustrative material respecting significant Presidential documents and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual Public Papers should be book-divided as needed, bound/styled suitably for the President's office, and include proper indexing and ancillary illustrative materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of prior years for Presidential Papers (§10.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Committee may authorize the publication of volumes of papers of the Presidents covering specified years before 1945 after consulting with the National Historical Publications and Records Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of historical presidential papers (pre-1945) requires Administrative Committee authorization and consultation with the NHPRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscription sales policy (§11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government Printing Office produces the paper and microfiche editions ... and the Superintendent of Documents ... makes them available for sale to the public. All fees are payable in advance ... They are not available for free distribution to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper and microfiche editions are sold to the public; fees must be prepaid; no free public distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register subscription pricing and online availability (§11.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription price for the paper edition of the daily FEDERAL REGISTER is $749 per year. Combined subscription price to the daily FR, monthly FR Index, and monthly LSA is $808 per year for paper, or $165 per year for microfiche. Six-month subscriptions available at one-half annual rate. Single copy prices based on page counts ($11 for <200 pages; $22 for 200–400; $33 for >400). Microfiche single issues $3. Online edition of the FEDERAL REGISTER is available on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified subscription and single-issue prices apply for paper and microfiche; online edition available via GPO Access. Prices exclude postage; prevailing postal rates apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Federal Regulations subscription pricing and online availability (§11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscription price for a complete set of the Code of Federal Regulations is $1,019 per year for bound paper edition, or $247 per year for microfiche. Government Printing Office sells individual volumes at prices determined by the Superintendent of Documents. The online edition of the Code of Federal Regulations is available on GPO Access (44 U.S.C. 4101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified subscription rates for CFR; online edition available via GPO Access; individual-volume pricing set by Superintendent of Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States Government Manual availability and sale (§11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The online edition of the Manual ... is available through the Government Printing Office’s Web site. Copies of a bound, paper edition of the Manual may be sold at a price determined by the Superintendent of Documents under the general direction of the Administrative Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government Manual available online via GPO; bound paper copies sold at Superintendent-determined price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Papers sale (§11.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of annual clothbound volumes are sold at a price determined by the Superintendent of Documents under the general direction of the Administrative Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Papers annual volumes are sold at prices set by the Superintendent of Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Register Index and LSA pricing (§11.7–11.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual subscription price for the monthly FEDERAL REGISTER Index, purchased separately in paper form, is $29. The annual subscription price for the monthly LSA (List of CFR Sections Affected), purchased separately in paper form, is $30. Prices exclude postage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate paper subscriptions for Index and LSA available at specified annual prices; postage excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of the Federal Register (§12.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the daily FEDERAL REGISTER in paper or microfiche form shall be made available without charge to Members of Congress (each Senator and each Member provided with not more than five copies based on written request), Congressional committees (number needed for official use based on written request), the Supreme Court, other constitutional or legislative courts, and Executive agencies (number needed for official use based on written request). Requisitions for quantity overruns are available to agencies (advance printing and binding requisition on Standard Form 1 must be submitted to GPO, received no later than 12 noon on the working day before publication). Agencies may request overruns of separate part issues with similar SF-1 procedures. Agencies may order limited quantities of extra copies to be paid for by the agency. Copies of the Federal Register Index and LSA are included with each official distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define entitlement for free official distribution (limits for Members), procedures and deadlines for ordering overruns (SF-1 before noon day prior), policies for separate parts and for paid extra copies; include Index and LSA with official distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of the Code of Federal Regulations (§12.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Code of Federal Regulations in paper or microfiche form shall be made available without charge to congressional committees, Supreme Court, other constitutional and legislative courts, and executive agencies (not to exceed 300 copies of individual titles per agency), based on written requests. Agencies may obtain additional copies at cost by submission before the press run of a printing and binding requisition (Standard Form 1). After the press run, requests for extra copies must be addressed to the Superintendent of Documents and paid for by the requesting agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official free distribution entitlements (with 300-copy per-title cap for agencies), process for ordering additional copies at cost (SF-1 before press run) and post-press-run ordering/payment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents (§12.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents shall be made available without charge to Members of Congress, Congressional committees, the Supreme Court, other constitutional and legislative courts, and Executive agencies, based on written requests. Legislative, judicial, and executive agencies may obtain additional copies at cost by submission before the press run of a printing and binding requisition to the Government Printing Office on Standard Form 1. After the press run, each request for extra copies of selected issues must be addressed to the Superintendent of Documents, to be paid for by the agency making the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same entitlement and SF-1 ordering/payment procedures as other official publications; free distribution to specified government recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official distribution of Public Papers of the Presidents (§12.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States shall be made available without charge to Members of Congress (one copy of each annual publication published during the Member's term in office based on written request), the Supreme Court (not more than 12 copies), and Executive agencies (each head provided with one copy of each annual publication based on written request). Agencies may obtain additional copies at cost before the press run (SF-1), and after the press run extra copies must be requested from the Superintendent and paid for by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify per-recipient entitlements (one copy per Member per annual publication; Supreme Court cap of 12 copies; one copy to each agency head) and procedures for ordering additional paid copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation: services to Federal agencies (§15.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall assist each agency in complying with the pertinent publication laws to assure efficient public service in promulgating administrative documents having the effect of legal notice or of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR must provide assistance to agencies to ensure legal and efficient promulgation of administrative documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information services (§15.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall provide for the answering of each appropriate inquiry presented in person, by telephone, or in writing. Each written communication and each matter involving the Administrative Committee shall be sent to the Director, Office of the Federal Register, National Archives and Records Administration, Washington, DC 20408.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR must maintain information services and designate the Director as the recipient for written communications/inquiries and Administrative Committee matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff assistance (§15.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The staff of the Office of the Federal Register shall provide informal assistance and advice to officials of the various agencies with respect to general or specific programs of regulatory drafting, procedures, and promulgation practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR staff should provide informal drafting and promulgation advice to agency officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduction and certification of copies (§15.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register shall furnish to requesting agencies, at cost, reproductions or certified copies of original acts and documents filed with that Office that are needed for official use unless funds are appropriated for that purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR will supply reproductions/certified copies at cost unless funded otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information on drafting and publication; instruction programs (§15.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Federal Register may prepare, and distribute to agencies, information and instructions designed to promote effective compliance with the purposes of chapter 15 of title 44, United States Code, sections 552–553 of title 5, United States Code, related statutes, and this chapter. The Director may also develop and conduct programs of technical instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFR has authority to issue drafting/publication guidance and to conduct technical instruction programs to aid agency compliance with applicable statutes and rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agency representatives (§16.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall designate, from its officers or employees, persons to serve in the following capacities with relation to the Office of the Federal Register: (1) A liaison officer and an alternate. (2) A certifying officer and an alternate. (3) An authorizing officer and an alternate. The same person may be designated to serve in one or more of these positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must name liaison, certifying, and authorizing officers (and alternates); one person may serve multiple roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for choosing liaison officer and notification (§16.1(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In choosing its liaison officer, each agency should consider that this officer will be the main contact between that agency and the Office of the Federal Register and that the liaison officer will be charged with the duties set forth in §16.2. Therefore, the agency should choose a person who is directly involved in the agency’s regulatory program. Each agency shall notify the Director of the name, title, address, and telephone number of each person it designates ... and shall promptly notify the Director of any changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a liaison who is directly involved in the agency's regulatory program and promptly provide and update contact information to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison duties (§16.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency liaison officer shall represent the agency in all matters relating to the submission of documents to the Office of the Federal Register, and respecting general compliance with this chapter; be responsible for the effective distribution and use within the agency of Federal Register information on document drafting and publication assistance authorized by §15.10; promote the agency’s participation in the technical instruction authorized by §15.10; and be available to discuss documents submitted for publication with the editors of the FEDERAL REGISTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaison officers act as primary agency contacts for document submission/compliance, internal distribution of drafting/publication guidance, promotion of technical instruction participation, and discussion with FR editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifying duties (§16.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency certifying officer is responsible for attaching the required number of true copies of each original document submitted by the agency to the Office of the Federal Register and for making the certification required by §§18.5 and 18.6 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifying officers must attach required true copies and execute required certifications per §§18.5–18.6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorizing duties (§16.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency authorizing officer is responsible for furnishing, to the Director of the Federal Register, a current mailing list of officers or employees of the agency who are authorized to receive the FEDERAL REGISTER, the Code of Federal Regulations, and the Weekly Compilation of Presidential Documents for official use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizing officers must provide and keep current the agency mailing list of personnel authorized to receive official publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and processing hours and confidentiality (§17.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless special arrangements are made with the Director of the Federal Register, the Office of the Federal Register receives documents only during official working hours. Upon receipt, each document shall be held for confidential processing until it is filed for public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are accepted only during official hours (unless arranged otherwise) and remain confidential while processed until filed for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and timing for regular schedule (§17.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document received shall be filed for public inspection only after it has been received, processed and assigned a publication date. Except as provided in paragraph (d), each document received by 2:00 p.m. which meets the requirements of this chapter shall be assigned to the regular schedule. Documents received after 2:00 p.m. which meet the requirements shall be assigned to the next working day's regular schedule. The regular schedule maps receipt-before-2:00 p.m. to filing-for-public-inspection and publication days (e.g., Monday received → filed Wednesday → published Thursday; Tuesday → filed Thursday → published Friday; Wednesday → filed Friday → published Monday; Thursday → filed Monday → published Tuesday; Friday → filed Tuesday → published Wednesday). Where a legal Federal holiday intervenes, one additional work day is added. Notices of meeting issued under the Government in the Sunshine Act are placed on immediate public inspection after received, processed, and assigned a publication date: notices received before 4:00 p.m. scheduled to be published 2 working days later; notices received after 4:00 p.m. scheduled to be published 3 working days later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 2:00 p.m. cutoff for regular schedule assignment and the provided weekday filing/publication mapping; observe holiday adjustments. Sunshine Act meeting notices have immediate public-inspection priority with specific 4:00 p.m. receipt rules and accelerated publication timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for emergency publication (§17.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart C addresses criteria for emergency publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section establishes that there are separate criteria for emergency publication (full text of criteria located in §17.3 and following provisions of Subpart C).
